title: Thornton v. Westminster Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained both challenges: Presbytery erred by refusing to place Memorial PCA’s call in Thornton’s hands and by initiating divestiture without censure. It reversed the divestiture decision and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date.
first_summary: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to approve his call and its initiation of administrative divestiture. The SJC sustained the complaint, reversed the divestiture decision, and ordered Presbytery to approve the call and arrange his installation because the valid call precluded BCO 34-10 divestiture.
summary: Thornton challenged Westminster Presbytery’s refusal to place Memorial PCA Session’s call in his hands and its simultaneous initiation of administrative divestiture without censure. The SJC sustained both issues, reversed the divestiture decision, and remanded with directions to approve and deliver the call and set an installation date. A valid call supplied the congregational approbation whose absence BCO 34-10’s administrative remedy requires; Presbytery also could not rely on undisclosed concerns while avoiding required judicial process. The ruling found clear error, not an absence of all presbyterial review authority.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case caption and SJC identity appear at lines 1–3 and 13; the full SJC approved the revised reasoning at lines 112–116 (printed pp. 85, 88).
evidence_notes.dispute: The two issues challenged refusal to deliver the call and initiation of BCO 34-10 divestiture, lines 49–59 (printed p. 86).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both issues were answered yes; the valid call barred administrative divestiture, and withholding approval to avoid judicial process was constitutional error, lines 55–108 (printed pp. 86–88). Relief appears at lines 108–110.
evidence_notes.qualifications: The majority did not decide whether citing BCO 20-10 rather than 21-1 was itself fatal, line 93; it found clear error in the exercise of review authority, lines 93–108 (printed pp. 87–88).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference. Later concurrences and the objection are separate writings, beginning at lines 120, 255, and 302.
